Markets face a defining week dominated by Nvidia's ([NVDA](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/NVDA/overview)) Wednesday earnings, an event that could determine the trajectory of AI infrastructure investment narratives and broader technology sector leadership heading into year-end. The AI chip leader's results and forward guidance will be scrutinized for evidence that massive data center spending can sustain current momentum or if concerns about returns on AI capital expenditures are beginning to materialize. The week also features critical retail earnings from Home Depot ([HD](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/HD/overview)) Tuesday, Target ([TGT](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/TGT/overview)) Wednesday, and Walmart ([WMT](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/WMT/overview)) Thursday that will provide comprehensive insights into consumer spending health as the crucial holiday shopping season approaches. The delayed release of September's jobs report continues to deprive markets of critical employment data, though Friday's Manufacturing and Services PMI reports will offer some perspective on business conditions. Wednesday's FOMC meeting minutes will provide detailed insights into the Federal Reserve's recent policy deliberations and December rate cut expectations.

Here are 5 things to watch this week in the Market.

**Nvidia's AI Infrastructure Inflection Point**

Wednesday's Nvidia ([NVDA](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/NVDA/overview)) earnings represent the most consequential corporate event of the quarter, serving as the ultimate litmus test for whether AI infrastructure investment can justify current market valuations and continue driving technology sector leadership. The results will be scrutinized for data center revenue growth, Hopper and Blackwell chip demand, and management's guidance about future AI accelerator sales. Nvidia's commentary on customer inventory levels, competition from custom chips developed by hyperscalers, and the sustainability of current AI investment cycles will be particularly important given recent technology stock volatility. Gross margins will be watched for any signs of pricing pressure, while China exposure amid trade tensions adds complexity. Gaming and automotive segment performance will provide context about business diversification beyond data centers. Given Nvidia's massive market capitalization and AI leadership role, the post-earnings reaction could significantly influence semiconductor stocks, cloud computing companies, and the broader technology sector that has driven much of this year's market gains.

**Retail Earnings Trilogy: Consumer Spending Reality Check**

The week delivers a comprehensive assessment of consumer health through three retail giants representing different consumer segments. Tuesday's Home Depot ([HD](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/HD/overview)) earnings will provide insights into home improvement spending and big-ticket purchase appetite, particularly important for assessing whether elevated mortgage rates are constraining housing-related spending. Wednesday's Target ([TGT](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/TGT/overview)) earnings will offer perspective on middle-income consumer health and discretionary spending trends heading into the critical holiday season. Target's commentary about traffic patterns, basket sizes, and category performance will help determine whether consumers are trading down or maintaining spending levels. Thursday's Walmart ([WMT](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/WMT/overview)) results will round out the consumer picture with insights into value-seeking behavior, grocery inflation trends, and e-commerce growth. All three retailers' holiday season guidance will be closely watched for clues about expected consumer demand through year-end.

**Chinese Consumer and Technology Dynamics**

Tuesday's earnings from PDD ([PDD](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/PDD/overview)) and Baidu ([BIDU](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/BIDU/overview)) will provide critical perspectives on Chinese consumer behavior and technology sector health amid ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions. PDD's results will offer insights into value-focused e-commerce demand and international expansion through platforms like Temu targeting Western consumers. Baidu's earnings will provide perspective on Chinese search advertising, autonomous driving technology, and AI cloud services beyond core search. Both companies' commentary about Chinese consumer confidence, regulatory environment, and government stimulus impacts will be important given questions about China's economic recovery. The results take on added significance amid trade war uncertainties and rare-earth export restrictions creating tensions between the world's two largest economies.

**Fed Minutes and Economic Activity Assessment**

Wednesday's FOMC meeting minutes at 2:00pm will provide detailed insights into the Federal Reserve's recent policy discussions, offering clues about internal debates regarding the December rate cut decision. The minutes will be analyzed for discussion about the appropriate pace of accommodation and evolving labor market assessments. Given the delayed September jobs report due to government shutdown, the minutes may reveal how policymakers are navigating decisions with incomplete employment data. Thursday delivers a dual snapshot of economic conditions with the Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index at 8:30am providing regional industrial perspectives and existing home sales at 10:00am offering insights into residential real estate activity amid elevated mortgage rates. Friday's Manufacturing and Services PMI data at 9:45am will provide comprehensive forward-looking insights into business activity across both goods-producing and services sectors. These activity indicators take on heightened importance as markets seek to fill the information gap created by delayed government employment data, with strong readings potentially reducing urgency for December rate cuts while weakness could reinforce dovish expectations.

**Healthcare Technology and Cybersecurity Spending**

Tuesday's Medtronic ([MDT](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/MDT/overview)) earnings will provide insights into medical device demand and hospital capital equipment spending. The company's diverse product portfolio spanning cardiac devices, surgical technologies, and diabetes management will offer comprehensive healthcare spending perspectives. Wednesday's Palo Alto Networks ([PANW](https://www.barchart.com/stocks/quotes/PANW/overview)) earnings represent a critical test for the cybersecurity sector, providing insights into enterprise security spending and cloud security adoption. Palo Alto's commentary on AI-powered security tools, zero-trust architecture demand, and competitive dynamics will be closely watched. The company's guidance about enterprise IT security budgets will help determine whether cybersecurity spending can remain resilient despite broader economic uncertainties. Both companies operate in sectors that tend to be less economically sensitive, making their results useful for assessing whether essential technology and healthcare investments are holding up.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            1. **Current Market Data**:

               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "Micron financial news latest week"
               Search: "Micron analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 5 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "Micron PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios

            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)

            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS

            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]

            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. **Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

# Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Gains as Next Full Self-Driving (Supervised) Version Rolls Out

[Steve Anderson](/news/author/steveanderson)

Story Highlights

Tesla rolls out a new version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised), which may be the one that goes live. Meanwhile, a new Supercharger station not owned by Tesla opens up.

Exciting news emerged for those who follow [electric vehicle](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/electric-vehicles) giant Tesla [(TSLA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla) and its attempts to have cars drive themselves. The latest version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is set to go live, and with it, the potential for wide release. That was welcome enough news for investors, who sent Tesla shares up nearly 1.5% in Friday afternoon’s trading.

The new version, FSD 14.2, will come with a range of upgrades and new features. The system now boasts improvements in parking behavior, handling emergency vehicles, a new kind of vision encoder, and improvements in routing, along with [general improvements](https://www.tipranks.com/news/teslas-fsd-is-truly-impressive-says-top-analyst-and-reaffirms-500-price-target) in driving behavior. The system can now better address what happens when an emergency vehicle shows up, offering “controlled pull-overs” as well as new yield functions.

The system has also been improved to better handle lane changes, school buses, and even unprotected turns. The improvements here, along with remarks from Tesla back in October, suggest that a wide release of Full Self-Driving might be in the making after all. In fact, some users even remark that FSD 14 handles driving tasks better than some humans do, which is, admittedly, kind of a low bar.

## **Third-Party Superchargers**

Most gas stations in the United States are not the property of the oil company that supplies them. Rather, they are [third-party owned](https://www.tipranks.com/news/tesla-stock-extends-its-november-rout-as-retail-investors-absorb-the-blow), more franchises than anything. Now, Tesla looks to branch out in similar fashion, and the first Supercharger station owned by a third party has gone live.

The station in question is located in Land O’Lakes, Florida. It is an eight-stall station, located at a Suncoast Charging facility, and is currently open for public use. Tesla, meanwhile, manages the station. It appears in the apps, and the navigation system, but someone else bought the hardware and paid for installation.

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

# Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Gains as Next Full Self-Driving (Supervised) Version Rolls Out

[Steve Anderson](/news/author/steveanderson)

Story Highlights

Tesla rolls out a new version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised), which may be the one that goes live. Meanwhile, a new Supercharger station not owned by Tesla opens up.

Exciting news emerged for those who follow [electric vehicle](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/electric-vehicles) giant Tesla [(TSLA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla) and its attempts to have cars drive themselves. The latest version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is set to go live, and with it, the potential for wide release. That was welcome enough news for investors, who sent Tesla shares up nearly 1.5% in Friday afternoon’s trading.

### TipRanks Black Friday Sale

* [Subscribe to TipRanks' Smart Investor Picks](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-smartinvestor/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  and see our data in action through our high-performing model portfolio -  now also 60% off

The new version, FSD 14.2, will come with a range of upgrades and new features. The system now boasts improvements in parking behavior, handling emergency vehicles, a new kind of vision encoder, and improvements in routing, along with [general improvements](https://www.tipranks.com/news/teslas-fsd-is-truly-impressive-says-top-analyst-and-reaffirms-500-price-target) in driving behavior. The system can now better address what happens when an emergency vehicle shows up, offering “controlled pull-overs” as well as new yield functions.

The system has also been improved to better handle lane changes, school buses, and even unprotected turns. The improvements here, along with remarks from Tesla back in October, suggest that a wide release of Full Self-Driving might be in the making after all. In fact, some users even remark that FSD 14 handles driving tasks better than some humans do, which is, admittedly, kind of a low bar.

## **Third-Party Superchargers**

Most gas stations in the United States are not the property of the oil company that supplies them. Rather, they are [third-party owned](https://www.tipranks.com/news/tesla-stock-extends-its-november-rout-as-retail-investors-absorb-the-blow), more franchises than anything. Now, Tesla looks to branch out in similar fashion, and the first Supercharger station owned by a third party has gone live.

The station in question is located in Land O’Lakes, Florida. It is an eight-stall station, located at a Suncoast Charging facility, and is currently open for public use. Tesla, meanwhile, manages the station. It appears in the apps, and the navigation system, but someone else bought the hardware and paid for installation.

## **Is Tesla a Buy, Hold or Sell?**

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on TSLA stock based on 14 Buys, 10 Holds, and 10 Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. After a 12.1% [rally in its share price](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla) over the past year, the [average TSLA price target](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla/forecast) of $383.37 per share implies 3.71% downside risk.

# What to Expect in Markets This Week: Retail Sales; Earnings From Deere, Dell and Alibaba; and Thanksgiving

![Terry Lane]()
![Terry Lane](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/ndol2zcoNBDh-qImvkfrfdtkIAI=/200x200/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/TerryHeadshotcrop-2e42cd194b404f6da48715967dd2c5de.jpg)

Terry Lane is a writer for Investopedia with 25 years of experience in journalism and communications. He covers personal finance, Congress, government regulations, and economics.

![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)
![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)

David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.
