# Here are Friday's biggest analyst calls: Tesla, Apple, Micron, Penn, Bank of America, CoreWeave & more

[Michael Bloom](https://www.cnbc.com/michael-bloom/)

[WATCH LIVE](/live-tv/)

Here are the biggest calls on Wall Street on Friday: Cantor Fitzgerald upgrades Ouster to overweight from neutral Cantor upgraded the autonomous vehicle solutions company following earnings. "We are encouraged by the acceleration of automotive-/autonomy-related revenue, and we expect OUST to continue to ramp up its deployments to self-driving vehicles and autonomous delivery robots across the U.S., particularly via its partnership with Serve Robotics (SERV, [overweight]) and May Mobility (private), among others." Citi upgrades Sonic Automotive to buy from neutral Citi says to buy the dip in the auto retailer. "The industry and company specific headwinds in 3Q, in our view, will turn positive in 4Q, creating a near-term buying opportunity for the stock. We upgraded SAH to Buy from Neutral with an $82 price target." Jefferies reiterates CoreWeave as buy Jefferies calls the stock "very attractive." "We see an attractive risk/reward profile, with CRWV now trading at 17x our rolled-forward EV/CY27 EBIT, compared to MSFT, AMZN, and ORCL..." UBS reiterates Apple as neutral UBS says it sees Apple as a beneficiary in the wearable technology space for personalized nutrition. "We see ready-to-eat / recipe box companies such as Hello Fresh, and wearable tech companies such as Apple to be the largest beneficiaries of the shift towards truly personalized nutrition." Deutsche Bank upgrades Baidu to buy from hold Deutsche says the China tech company is well positioned for artificial intelligence. " Baidu has established a set of leading AI businesses spanning cloud computing, robotaxis, intelligent search, and AI chips." Read more. Morgan Stanley names Bank of America top pick Morgan Stanley says a "new period of consecutive [operating] leverage has arrived." "We move BAC to our Top Pick in LC [large cap] Banks post investor day where mgmt outlined a clear path to 16-18% ROTCE, driven by revenue growth and expense ratio improvement to 55-59%." Bank of America upgrades Globus Medical to buy from neutral Bank of America sees "compounding profits" for the med tech company. "We are upgrading GMED to Buy from Neutral." Barclays reiterates Tesla as equal weight Barclays says Tesla still needs to work on its growth initiatives following Thursday's shareholder vote. "While there were few surprises at today's Tesla AGM, the event broadly reminded us of the excitement investors face ahead on Tesla's growth prospects. Yet we believe the key question for the stock now remains on the execution path for Tesla's growth initiatives." Macquarie upgrades Unity to outperform from neutral Macquarie says in an upgrade of Unity that the software company is well positioned for growth. "Mgmt's execution has been solid and we have greater confidence in the long-term growth opportunity driving increased FCF and operating leverage." Rothschild & Co Redburn upgrades ASML to buy from hold Rothschild says the semiconductor equipment maker is firing on all cylinders. "ASML's earnings outlook is further supported by the strong upcycle in AI-fueled chip demand." Oppenheimer upgrades JFrog to outperform from perform The firm upgrades the stock following earnings. "We're upgrading JFrog to Outperform from Perform, raising our revenue estimates, and establishing a $75 price target following another strong quarter of upside and accelerating Cloud growth." Wells Fargo reiterates Micron Technology as buy Wells Fargo raises its price target on Micron to $300 per share from $220. "This week we hosted meetings w/ CEO, Sanjay Mehrotra & EVP, Global Operations, Manish Bhatia. Mtgs reinforce +thesis on MU's execution / competitive position (HBM4 confidence) & memory industry dynamics. Increase ests; PT to $300." KeyBanc upgrades Datadog to overweight from sector weight Key upgrades the stock following earnings. "We upgrade shares of DDOG to Overweight as the two areas of concern that kept us Sector Weight materialized positively: 1) revenue ex. OpenAI accelerated, and the strength was broad based; and 2) visibility into sustained OpenAI spend for the next several quarters after renewing/expanding its commitment in 3Q." Wolfe upgrades Matson to outperform from peer perform Wolfe upgrades the shipping and logistics company following earnings. "As evidenced by its 3Q report and 4Q guide, MATX's pricing is again de-coupling from industry spot rates. Thus, we have increased confidence in $10+ of normalized EPS, and with a discounted valuation, we're raising our rating to Outperform." JPMorgan adds GE Vernova to the focus list The bank says it sees an "attractive entry point." "We are adding GE Vernova to the J.P. Morgan US Equity Analyst Focus List (Growth) and placing the stock on Positive Catalyst Watch. The stock has underperformed power generation peers over the past two months, despite a solid 3Q print, which we believe creates a compelling entry point." Stifel upgrades Penn to buy from hold Stifel says the gambling company has an " attractive pipeline of growth projects. " "While recent underperformance partially factors concerns on the consumer & rising competitor promo spend, we see PENN as comparatively well-positioned given geographic diversification, well-documented operating prowess and relatively higher quality assets enabling PENN to compete primarily on product." Benchmark upgrades Trade Desk to buy from hold Benchmark upgrades the advertising stock following earnings and says the "pain" is already priced in. "We upgrade TTD to a Buy and establish a $65 DCF-based PT. While the stock still contends with macro uncertainties and awaits restructuring efficiencies to play out, our prior perceived relative industry growth hurdles are generally rearview." JPMorgan upgrades ArcelorMittal to overweight from neutral JPMorgan upgraded the steel company following earnings. " Mittal reported its Q3'25 results yesterday which gave a reassuring outlook for Q4, including guidance for a strong Q4 FCF and net debt reduction attributable to a $1.9bn working capital release."

            Collect the full data pack required for a comprehensive briefing.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            Collect the full data pack required for a comprehensive briefing.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            1. **Current Market Data**:

               Search: "Micron trading volume market data"
               Extract: Current price, daily change ($ and %), trading volume, 52-week range
            
            2. **Latest Earnings Information**:
               Search: "Micron latest quarterly earnings results"
               Search: "Micron earnings vs estimates beat miss"
               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "Micron financial news latest week"
               Search: "Micron analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 5 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "Micron PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)
            - Trading Volume: X.X million (vs avg X.X million)
            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Revenue: $XXX billion actual vs $XXX billion estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Year-over-Year Growth: X%
            - Quarter: QX YYYY
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            2. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            3. [Continue until you reach the required number of items]
            
            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS
            - P/E Ratio: XX.X
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - [Other available metrics]
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            **CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
            - Use EXACT figures, not approximations
            - Include source URLs for verification
            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

Overview Semiconductors / Technology\\n------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\nMicron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025\\n\\n[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)\\n\\n## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**\\n\\nU.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.\\n\\n### TipRanks Black Friday Sale\\n\\n* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.\\n* [Subscribe to TipRanks' Smart Investor Picks](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-smartinvestor/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  and see our data in action through our high-performing model portfolio -  now also 60% off\\n\\nEnergy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).\\n\\nThe latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.\\n\\n## **Nvidia\u2019s Strong Results Couldn\u2019t Stop the Slide**\\n\\nThe main story last week surrounded **Nvidia\u2019s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company\u2019s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains \u201coff the charts.\u201d\\n\\nDespite the strong results, Nvidia\u2019s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).\\n\\nThe reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.\\n\\n## **Stocks That Made the Week**\\n\\nWhile Nvidia\u2019s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI\u2019s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia\u2019s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.\\n\\nBitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.\\n\\nIn contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company\u2019s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.\\n\\nIn other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw\u2019s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.\\n\\nAlso in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company\u2019s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in \u201cservices from space\u201d companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.\\n\\n## **Crypto\u2019s Rough Week**\\n\\n**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.\\n\\nThe total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as \u201ca bit of a meltdown,\u201d adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.\\n\\n## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**\\n\\nThe earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.\\n\\nOn Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.\\n\\nOn Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.\\n\\nWednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.\\n\\nLater in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.\\n\\n### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**\\n\\nSeveral notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.\\n\\nOn Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson\u2019s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.\\n\\nTuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.\\n\\nOn Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.\\n\\nThese payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Gains as Next Full Self-Driving (Supervised) Version Rolls Out\\n\\n[Steve Anderson](/news/author/steveanderson)\\n\\nStory Highlights\\n\\nTesla rolls out a new version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised), which may be the one that goes live. Meanwhile, a new Supercharger station not owned by Tesla opens up.\\n\\nExciting news emerged for those who follow [electric vehicle](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/electric-vehicles) giant Tesla [(TSLA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla) and its attempts to have cars drive themselves. The latest version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is set to go live, and with it, the potential for wide release. That was welcome enough news for investors, who sent Tesla shares up nearly 1.5% in Friday afternoon\u2019s trading.\\n\\n### TipRanks Black Friday Sale\\n\\n* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.\\n* [Subscribe to TipRanks' Smart Investor Picks](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-smartinvestor/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  and see our data in action through our high-performing model portfolio -  now also 60% off\\n\\nThe new version, FSD 14.2, will come with a range of upgrades and new features. The system now boasts improvements in parking behavior, handling emergency vehicles, a new kind of vision encoder, and improvements in routing, along with [general improvements](https://www.tipranks.com/news/teslas-fsd-is-truly-impressive-says-top-analyst-and-reaffirms-500-price-target) in driving behavior. The system can now better address what happens when an emergency vehicle shows up, offering \u201ccontrolled pull-overs\u201d as well as new yield functions.\\n\\nThe system has also been improved to better handle lane changes, school buses, and even unprotected turns. The improvements here, along with remarks from Tesla back in October, suggest that a wide release of Full Self-Driving might be in the making after all. In fact, some users even remark that FSD 14 handles driving tasks better than some humans do, which is, admittedly, kind of a low bar.\\n\\n## **Third-Party Superchargers**\\n\\nMost gas stations in the United States are not the property of the oil company that supplies them. Rather, they are [third-party owned](https://www.tipranks.com/news/tesla-stock-extends-its-november-rout-as-retail-investors-absorb-the-blow), more franchises than anything. Now, Tesla looks to branch out in similar fashion, and the first Supercharger station owned by a third party has gone live.\\n\\nThe station in question is located in Land O\u2019Lakes, Florida. It is an eight-stall station, located at a Suncoast Charging facility, and is currently open for public use. Tesla, meanwhile, manages the station. He covers personal finance, Congress, government regulations, and economics.\\n\\n![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)\\n![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)\\n\\nDavid Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images\\n\\nThis trading week is\u2014Thankfully\u2014shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.\\n\\nStock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.\\n\\nThe September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year.\u00a0Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.\\n\\nIn addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.\\n\\nRead to the bottom for our calendar of key events\u2014and one more thing.\\n\\n## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week\\n\\nInvestors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.\\n\\nTuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).\\n\\nDell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components.\u00a0John Deere\u2019s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).\\n\\n## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday\\n\\n[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.\\n\\nReports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week\u2019s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).\\n\\nSeveral reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.\\n\\nQuick Links: [Recap Last Week\u2019s Trading](https://www.investopedia.com/dow-jones-today-11212025-11854331) | [Read Investopedia\u2019s Latest News](https://www.investopedia.com/news-4427706)\\n\\n## This Week\u2019s Calendar\\n\\n**Monday, Nov. 24**\\n\\n**Tuesday, Nov. 25**\\n\\n**Wednesday, Nov. 26**\\n\\n**Thursday, Nov. 27**\\n\\n**Friday, Nov. 28**\\n\\n## One More Thing\\n\\nWondering if ChatGPT has the answers for your questions about where to invest $10,000? attributes.llm.request.functions.3.description: Crawl multiple pages from a website starting from a base URL. Use this tool when you need to gather information from multiple related pages across a website or explore a site's structure. It follows internal links and extracts content from multiple pages, but truncates content to 500 characters per page. For full content extraction, use tavily_map to discover URLs first, then tavily_extract to get complete content from specific pages. Useful for comprehensive research on documentation sites, blogs, or when you need to understand the full scope of information available on a website.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

# Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Gains as Next Full Self-Driving (Supervised) Version Rolls Out

[Steve Anderson](/news/author/steveanderson)

Story Highlights

Tesla rolls out a new version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised), which may be the one that goes live. Meanwhile, a new Supercharger station not owned by Tesla opens up.

Exciting news emerged for those who follow [electric vehicle](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/electric-vehicles) giant Tesla [(TSLA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla) and its attempts to have cars drive themselves. The latest version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is set to go live, and with it, the potential for wide release. That was welcome enough news for investors, who sent Tesla shares up nearly 1.5% in Friday afternoon’s trading.

The new version, FSD 14.2, will come with a range of upgrades and new features. The system now boasts improvements in parking behavior, handling emergency vehicles, a new kind of vision encoder, and improvements in routing, along with [general improvements](https://www.tipranks.com/news/teslas-fsd-is-truly-impressive-says-top-analyst-and-reaffirms-500-price-target) in driving behavior. The system can now better address what happens when an emergency vehicle shows up, offering “controlled pull-overs” as well as new yield functions.

The system has also been improved to better handle lane changes, school buses, and even unprotected turns. The improvements here, along with remarks from Tesla back in October, suggest that a wide release of Full Self-Driving might be in the making after all. In fact, some users even remark that FSD 14 handles driving tasks better than some humans do, which is, admittedly, kind of a low bar.

## **Third-Party Superchargers**

Most gas stations in the United States are not the property of the oil company that supplies them. Rather, they are [third-party owned](https://www.tipranks.com/news/tesla-stock-extends-its-november-rout-as-retail-investors-absorb-the-blow), more franchises than anything. Now, Tesla looks to branch out in similar fashion, and the first Supercharger station owned by a third party has gone live.

The station in question is located in Land O’Lakes, Florida. It is an eight-stall station, located at a Suncoast Charging facility, and is currently open for public use. Tesla, meanwhile, manages the station. It appears in the apps, and the navigation system, but someone else bought the hardware and paid for installation.

## **Is Tesla a Buy, Hold or Sell?**

After a 12.1% [rally in its share price](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla) over the past year, the [average TSLA price target](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tsla/forecast) of $383.37 per share implies 3.71% downside risk.

![Terry Lane]()
![Terry Lane](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/ndol2zcoNBDh-qImvkfrfdtkIAI=/200x200/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/TerryHeadshotcrop-2e42cd194b404f6da48715967dd2c5de.jpg)

Terry Lane is a writer for Investopedia with 25 years of experience in journalism and communications. He covers personal finance, Congress, government regulations, and economics.

![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)
![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)

David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

Latest Business & Market News

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

* [AAPL](/quote/AAPL)

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Shares of the chipmaker witnessed a gain of 1.18% over the previous month, beating the performance of the Computer and Technology sector with its gain of 0.07%, and the S&P 500's loss of 0.31%.

The investment community will be closely monitoring the performance of Micron in its forthcoming earnings report. The company is scheduled to release its earnings on December 17, 2025. Simultaneously, our latest consensus estimate expects the revenue to be $12.54 billion, showing a 43.97% escalation compared to the year-ago quarter.

Looking at the full year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates suggest analysts are expecting earnings of $17.17 per share and revenue of $54.77 billion. These totals would mark changes of +107.12% and +46.52%, respectively, from last year.

Any recent changes to analyst estimates for Micron should also be noted by investors. Recent revisions tend to reflect the latest near-term business trends. With this in mind, we can consider positive estimate revisions a sign of optimism about the business outlook.

Our research demonstrates that these adjustments in estimates directly associate with imminent stock price performance. To exploit this, we've formed the Zacks Rank, a quantitative model that includes these estimate changes and presents a viable rating system.

The Zacks Rank system, stretching from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), has a noteworthy track record of outperforming, validated by third-party audits, with stocks rated #1 producing an average annual return of +25% since the year 1988. Within the past 30 days, our consensus EPS projection has moved 6.85% higher. Micron presently features a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy).

Valuation is also important, so investors should note that Micron has a Forward P/E ratio of 13.08 right now. Its industry sports an average Forward P/E of 23.56, so one might conclude that Micron is trading at a discount comparatively.

Also, we should mention that MU has a PEG ratio of 0.46. Comparable to the widely accepted P/E ratio, the PEG ratio also accounts for the company's projected earnings growth. The Computer - Integrated Systems was holding an average PEG ratio of 1.04 at yesterday's closing price.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

**More AI Stocks:**

* [**Is Nvidia’s AI boom already priced in? Oppenheimer doesn’t think so**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/is-nvidias-ai-boom-already-priced-in-oppenheimer-doesnt-think-so)
* [**Windows president told ‘Stop this nonsense. No one wants this’**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/windows-president-told-stop-this-nonsense-no-one-wants-this)
* [**Michael Burry turns up heat on anti-AI bet**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/fund-manager-michael-burry-turns-up-heat-on-anti-ai-bet)
* [**AI plays expanding role in predicting natural disasters**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/ai-plays-expanding-role-in-predicting-natural-disasters)
* [**Morgan Stanley revamps Nvidia’s price target ahead of big Q3**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/morgan-stanley-revamps-nvidias-price-target-ahead-of-big-q3)
* [**Cathie Wood buys $16.2 million of sinking AI stock**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/cathie-wood-buys-16-2-million-of-sinking-ai-stock)

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

Latest Business & Market News

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

* [AAPL](/quote/AAPL)

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

The stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.

Aparajita Chatterjee writes about stocks making big moves during the trading day and on the week and daily closing updates on the major market indexes, including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite. Aparajita’s passion is research and finding the story behind the numbers. You can reach out to c-achatterjee@thearenagroup.net with your tips and suggestions.

Dana Sullivan Kilroy has been a writer and editor for more than 20 years. She covers travel, retail, technology, and Las Vegas entertainment for TheStreet. Her work has appeared in The New York Times, Real Simple, Self, Outside, BabyCenter, Everyday Health, and WebMD.
