Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

**More AI Stocks:**

* [**Is Nvidia’s AI boom already priced in? Oppenheimer doesn’t think so**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/is-nvidias-ai-boom-already-priced-in-oppenheimer-doesnt-think-so)
* [**Windows president told ‘Stop this nonsense. No one wants this’**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/windows-president-told-stop-this-nonsense-no-one-wants-this)
* [**Michael Burry turns up heat on anti-AI bet**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/fund-manager-michael-burry-turns-up-heat-on-anti-ai-bet)
* [**AI plays expanding role in predicting natural disasters**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/ai-plays-expanding-role-in-predicting-natural-disasters)
* [**Morgan Stanley revamps Nvidia’s price target ahead of big Q3**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/morgan-stanley-revamps-nvidias-price-target-ahead-of-big-q3)
* [**Cathie Wood buys $16.2 million of sinking AI stock**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/cathie-wood-buys-16-2-million-of-sinking-ai-stock)

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

* [AAPL](/quote/AAPL)

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

The stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

The stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

Shares of the chipmaker witnessed a gain of 1.18% over the previous month, beating the performance of the Computer and Technology sector with its gain of 0.07%, and the S&P 500's loss of 0.31%.

The investment community will be closely monitoring the performance of Micron in its forthcoming earnings report. The company is scheduled to release its earnings on December 17, 2025. The company is forecasted to report an EPS of $3.77, showcasing a 110.61% upward movement from the corresponding quarter of the prior year. Simultaneously, our latest consensus estimate expects the revenue to be $12.54 billion, showing a 43.97% escalation compared to the year-ago quarter.

Looking at the full year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates suggest analysts are expecting earnings of $17.17 per share and revenue of $54.77 billion. These totals would mark changes of +107.12% and +46.52%, respectively, from last year.

Any recent changes to analyst estimates for Micron should also be noted by investors. Recent revisions tend to reflect the latest near-term business trends. With this in mind, we can consider positive estimate revisions a sign of optimism about the business outlook.

Our research demonstrates that these adjustments in estimates directly associate with imminent stock price performance. To exploit this, we've formed the Zacks Rank, a quantitative model that includes these estimate changes and presents a viable rating system.

The Zacks Rank system, stretching from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), has a noteworthy track record of outperforming, validated by third-party audits, with stocks rated #1 producing an average annual return of +25% since the year 1988. Within the past 30 days, our consensus EPS projection has moved 6.85% higher. Micron presently features a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy).

Valuation is also important, so investors should note that Micron has a Forward P/E ratio of 13.08 right now. Its industry sports an average Forward P/E of 23.56, so one might conclude that Micron is trading at a discount comparatively.

Also, we should mention that MU has a PEG ratio of 0.46. Comparable to the widely accepted P/E ratio, the PEG ratio also accounts for the company's projected earnings growth. The Computer - Integrated Systems was holding an average PEG ratio of 1.04 at yesterday's closing price.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

**More AI Stocks:**

* [**Is Nvidia’s AI boom already priced in? Oppenheimer doesn’t think so**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/is-nvidias-ai-boom-already-priced-in-oppenheimer-doesnt-think-so)
* [**Windows president told ‘Stop this nonsense. No one wants this’**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/windows-president-told-stop-this-nonsense-no-one-wants-this)
* [**Michael Burry turns up heat on anti-AI bet**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/fund-manager-michael-burry-turns-up-heat-on-anti-ai-bet)
* [**AI plays expanding role in predicting natural disasters**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/ai-plays-expanding-role-in-predicting-natural-disasters)
* [**Morgan Stanley revamps Nvidia’s price target ahead of big Q3**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/morgan-stanley-revamps-nvidias-price-target-ahead-of-big-q3)
* [**Cathie Wood buys $16.2 million of sinking AI stock**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/cathie-wood-buys-16-2-million-of-sinking-ai-stock)

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

* [AAPL](/quote/AAPL)

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

The stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

**More AI Stocks:**

* [**Is Nvidia’s AI boom already priced in? Oppenheimer doesn’t think so**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/is-nvidias-ai-boom-already-priced-in-oppenheimer-doesnt-think-so)
* [**Windows president told ‘Stop this nonsense. No one wants this’**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/windows-president-told-stop-this-nonsense-no-one-wants-this)
* [**Michael Burry turns up heat on anti-AI bet**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/fund-manager-michael-burry-turns-up-heat-on-anti-ai-bet)
* [**AI plays expanding role in predicting natural disasters**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/ai-plays-expanding-role-in-predicting-natural-disasters)
* [**Morgan Stanley revamps Nvidia’s price target ahead of big Q3**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/morgan-stanley-revamps-nvidias-price-target-ahead-of-big-q3)
* [**Cathie Wood buys $16.2 million of sinking AI stock**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/cathie-wood-buys-16-2-million-of-sinking-ai-stock)

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

Latest Business & Market News

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

* [AAPL](/quote/AAPL)

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

The stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.

Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

The stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.

ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.\\n\\n### TipRanks Black Friday Sale\\n\\n* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.\\n* [Subscribe to TipRanks' Smart Investor Picks](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-smartinvestor/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  and see our data in action through our high-performing model portfolio -  now also 60% off\\n\\nEnergy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).\\n\\nThe latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.\\n\\n## **Nvidia\u2019s Strong Results Couldn\u2019t Stop the Slide**\\n\\nThe main story last week surrounded **Nvidia\u2019s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company\u2019s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains \u201coff the charts.\u201d\\n\\nDespite the strong results, Nvidia\u2019s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).\\n\\nThe reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.\\n\\n## **Stocks That Made the Week**\\n\\nWhile Nvidia\u2019s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI\u2019s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia\u2019s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.\\n\\nBitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.\\n\\nIn contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company\u2019s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.\\n\\nIn other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw\u2019s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.\\n\\nAlso in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company\u2019s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in \u201cservices from space\u201d companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.\\n\\n## **Crypto\u2019s Rough Week**\\n\\n**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.\\n\\nThe total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as \u201ca bit of a meltdown,\u201d adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.\\n\\n## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**\\n\\nThe earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.\\n\\nOn Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.\\n\\nOn Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.\\n\\nWednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.\\n\\nLater in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.\\n\\n### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**\\n\\nSeveral notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.\\n\\nOn Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson\u2019s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.\\n\\nTuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.\\n\\nOn Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.\\n\\nThese payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through Use this tool when you need to understand a website's organization, find specific pages, or get an overview of all available content without extracting the actual text. Returns a structured list of URLs and their relationships. Useful for site exploration, finding documentation pages, or understanding how a website is organized.

You are a comprehensive financial data collector for Micron.
            Collect the full data pack required for a comprehensive briefing.

            Use Tavily together with fetch to gather the requested facts in the order listed. Prefer the most recent data and stop once each section has concrete numbers.

            **REQUIRED DATA TO COLLECT:**
            
            1. **Current Market Data**:
               Search: "Micron stock price today current"
               Search: "Micron trading volume market data"
               Extract: Current price, daily change ($ and %), trading volume, 52-week range
            
            2. **Latest Earnings Information**:
               Search: "Micron latest quarterly earnings results"
               Search: "Micron earnings vs estimates beat miss"
               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "Micron financial news latest week"
               Search: "Micron analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 5 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "Micron PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)
            - Trading Volume: X.X million (vs avg X.X million)
            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Revenue: $XXX billion actual vs $XXX billion estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Year-over-Year Growth: X%
            - Quarter: QX YYYY
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            2. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            3. [Continue until you reach the required number of items]
            
            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS
            - P/E Ratio: XX.X
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - [Other available metrics]
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            **CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
            - Use EXACT figures, not approximations
            - Include source URLs for verification
            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found
