Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

Here are Thursday's biggest analyst calls: Nvidia, Micron, Nike, Cisco, Boeing, CoreWeave, Circle, Meta, AutoZone & more
========================================================================================================================

Published Thu, Nov 13 2025 8:24 AM EST

[Michael Bloom](https://www.cnbc.com/michael-bloom/)

[WATCH LIVE](https://www.cnbc.com/live-tv/)

Here are the biggest calls on Wall Street on Thursday: KeyBanc upgrades Carpenter Technology and ATI to overweight from sector weight KeyBanc says specialty metals companies have pricing power. "Amid recent margin performances and bottoming backlogs, we are upgrading ATI and CRS to Overweight (from Sector Weight)." Bernstein initiates Hesai at outperform Bernstein called the autonomous vehicle and humanoid light sensor company a "global leader." " Hesai is riding the wave of the intelligent vehicle boom." Morgan Stanley names Micron a top pick The investment bank raises its price target on Micron Technology to $325 per share from $220. "We are entering uncharted territory, as we have a 2018 style shortage forming but from a much higher EPS starting point; we expect serial upwards revisions to continue, as soon as next week." Read more. Oppenheimer reiterates Nvidia as outperform Oppenheimer raises its price target on the stock ahead of earnings next week. " NVDA remains best positioned to win in AI. Reiterate Outperform. Target to $265 (from $225)." Benchmark initiates Vital Farms as buy Benchmark says it's bullish on the egg company. "For long-term oriented investors, we believe Vital has a sustainable runway of double-digit growth that we believe is wholly overlooked at the current valuation. Goldman Sachs upgrades AutoZone to buy from neutral Goldman says investors should buy the dip in the auto parts retailer. "For AZO, we see a more attractive risk/reward following the recent selloff, and we expect AZO's domestic DIFM [do it for me] business will continue to take share, while DIY demand headwinds are likely to be temporary." Goldman Sachs downgrades Dollar Tree to sell from buy Goldman says it sees too many negative catalysts. "We are downgrading DLTR to Sell from Buy. DLTR's management team has worked hard to improve the company's positioning through its multi-price initiative and improved store conditions, which has resulted in better comp trends and improved margins." Wedbush adds Meta Platforms to best ideas list; upgrades Booking Holdings and DoorDash to outperform from neutral The investment bank says it sees more upside in Meta, Booking Holdings and DoorDash. "Post-results, we think the disconnect between fundamentals and investor sentiment offers attractive upside to META, BKNG , and DASH. With this report, we are adding META to the Wedbush Best Ideas List, and upgrading our ratings of BKNG and DASH to Outperform." Deutsche Bank upgrades FireFly Aerospace to buy from hold Deutsche says in its upgrade of FireFly that the space company is "ready to ignite." "We update our model, factoring in an updated launch and program win cadence; we also refine our SciTec contribution for the upcoming quarter/year. This takes our price target down by $10 to $30, still implying material upside from current levels and upgrade the stock from Hold to Buy." JPMorgan upgrades Circle Internet to overweight from underweight The firm double upgrades the stock following earnings. "We are upgrading Circle shares from Underweight to Overweight." Read more. Compass Point initiates CoreWeave as buy Compass says the company is "still the one to beat." "We are initiating coverage of CoreWeave ( CRWV) with a Buy." Wells Fargo upgrades Nike to overweight from equal weight Wells says the athletic shoe maker's visibility is improving. "Upgrade to OW and raise PT to $75. We feel the time has come where visibility into NKE's P & L direction (both on revs and margin) is finally improving." Bank of America reiterates Cisco as buy Bank of America raises its price target on Cisco to $95 per share from $85 following earnings. "The quarter's tale is about very strong orders for AI networking and a $3bn FY26 AI revenue target, vs. $1bn recorded in 2025." Oppenheimer initiates Rocket Companies as outperform Oppenheimer sees robust demand for the fintech company. "Initiating coverage of Rocket Companies (RKT) with an Outperform rating and a $25 target, representing 15x 2027E EBITDA." Bank of America upgrades Trane to buy from neutral Bank of America says the company should benefit from a "transport recovery" in 2026. "We upgrade our rating on Trane Technologies (TT) to Buy from Neutral: (1) Trane has executed well through the [residential] slowdown in 2H25 and should get the potential upside in 2026; (2) Trane should benefit from Americas Transport recovery in 2026." Bernstein reiterates Boeing as outperform Bernstein lowers its price target on the stock to $267 per share from $287. "After Boeing reported Q3 earnings on October 30th, the stock fell sharply even with above consensus revenues. Boeing reiterated that it is on track for 737 and 787 production ramps. We see those ramps as most important for the stock, despite the 777X delay impact. Boeing shares reacted negatively as investors became concerned about Capex levels and cash flow implications. Shares have not recovered." Argus upgrades Kimberly-Clark to buy from hold Argus says it likes the company's deal for Kenvue. "KMB manufactures and markets personal care and consumer tissue products worldwide. The company is making substantial changes to its portfolio, including the acquisition of Kenvue Inc., which will create the second largest health and wellness company globally and is expected to be accretive to earnings in the second year."

Citi upgrades Sonic Automotive to buy from neutral Citi says to buy the dip in the auto retailer. "We see an attractive risk/reward profile, with CRWV now trading at 17x our rolled-forward EV/CY27 EBIT, compared to MSFT, AMZN, and ORCL..." UBS reiterates Apple as neutral UBS says it sees Apple as a beneficiary in the wearable technology space for personalized nutrition. "We see ready-to-eat / recipe box companies such as Hello Fresh, and wearable tech companies such as Apple to be the largest beneficiaries of the shift towards truly personalized nutrition." Deutsche Bank upgrades Baidu to buy from hold Deutsche says the China tech company is well positioned for artificial intelligence. " Baidu has established a set of leading AI businesses spanning cloud computing, robotaxis, intelligent search, and AI chips." Read more. "We move BAC to our Top Pick in LC [large cap] Banks post investor day where mgmt outlined a clear path to 16-18% ROTCE, driven by revenue growth and expense ratio improvement to 55-59%." Bank of America upgrades Globus Medical to buy from neutral Bank of America sees "compounding profits" for the med tech company. "We are upgrading GMED to Buy from Neutral." Barclays reiterates Tesla as equal weight Barclays says Tesla still needs to work on its growth initiatives following Thursday's shareholder vote. "While there were few surprises at today's Tesla AGM, the event broadly reminded us of the excitement investors face ahead on Tesla's growth prospects. "Mgmt's execution has been solid and we have greater confidence in the long-term growth opportunity driving increased FCF and operating leverage." Rothschild & Co Redburn upgrades ASML to buy from hold Rothschild says the semiconductor equipment maker is firing on all cylinders. "ASML's earnings outlook is further supported by the strong upcycle in AI-fueled chip demand." Oppenheimer upgrades JFrog to outperform from perform The firm upgrades the stock following earnings. "We're upgrading JFrog to Outperform from Perform, raising our revenue estimates, and establishing a $75 price target following another strong quarter of upside and accelerating Cloud growth." Wells Fargo reiterates Micron Technology as buy Wells Fargo raises its price target on Micron to $300 per share from $220. "This week we hosted meetings w/ CEO, Sanjay Mehrotra & EVP, Global Operations, Manish Bhatia.                Search: "Micron financial news latest week"

            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS

Overview Semiconductors / Technology\\n------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\nMicron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. [Stocks](/investing/stocks)\\n\\n# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead\\n\\nHere is your daily stock market wrap.\\n\\nBy[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)\\n\\nStocks Writer, The Street\\n\\nReviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)\\n\\n[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)\\n\\n## Key Points\\n\\n* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.\\n* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.\\n* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.\\n\\nGood news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.\\n\\n* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**\\n* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**\\n* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**\\n\\nAfter weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.\\n\\nThe [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.\\n\\nIn commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.\\n\\nOil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.\\n\\n\u201cIs it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don\u2019t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,\u201d President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.\\n\\n## US-China talks boost investor confidence\\n\\nOn Monday, President Trump posted that he \u201chad a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.\u201d\\n\\nThe optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.\\n\\nIt was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.\\n\\nThe talks follow President Trump and Xi\u2019s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.\\n\\n## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally\\n\\nCipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.\\n\\n**More AI Stocks:**\\n\\n* [**Is Nvidia\u2019s AI boom already priced in? Oppenheimer doesn\u2019t think so**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/is-nvidias-ai-boom-already-priced-in-oppenheimer-doesnt-think-so)\\n* [**Windows president told \u2018Stop this nonsense. No one wants this\u2019**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/windows-president-told-stop-this-nonsense-no-one-wants-this)\\n* [**Michael Burry turns up heat on anti-AI bet**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/fund-manager-michael-burry-turns-up-heat-on-anti-ai-bet)\\n* [**AI plays expanding role in predicting natural disasters**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/ai-plays-expanding-role-in-predicting-natural-disasters)\\n* [**Morgan Stanley revamps Nvidia\u2019s price target ahead of big Q3**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/morgan-stanley-revamps-nvidias-price-target-ahead-of-big-q3)\\n* [**Cathie Wood buys $16.2 million of sinking AI stock**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/cathie-wood-buys-16-2-million-of-sinking-ai-stock)\\n\\nCipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.\\n\\nJPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company\u2019s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).\\n\\nThis upgrade follows Cipher Mining\u2019s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.\\n\\nThe transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.\\n\\nLatest Business & Market News\\n\\n## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)\\n\\nApple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.\\n\\nAparajita Chatterjee\\n\\n* [AAPL](/quote/AAPL)\\n\\nThe deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company\u2019s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.\\n\\nCipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) \u201cto use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.\u201d\\n\\n**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a \u201cflurry of deal activity\u201d and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).\\n\\n## Big tech and energy stock news\\n\\nApple\u2019s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.\\n\\nHowever, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple\u2019s briefing centers.\\n\\nIn an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company\u2019s stock was declining after hours.\\n\\nSeparately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan\u2019s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).\\n\\nCarl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.\\n\\nThe increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.\\n\\nThe stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.\\n\\nStocks\\n\\n## [Lutnick says President Trump holds keys to Nvidia\u2019s China future](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/secretary-lutnick-says-president-trump-holds-keys-to-nvidias-china-future)\\n\\nNvidia's sales in China hinge on a major Trump decision.\\n\\nTodd Campbell\\n\\n## About the authors\\n\\n## [Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)\\n\\nStocks Writer, The Street\\n\\nAparajita Chatterjee writes about stocks making big moves during the trading day and on the week and daily closing updates on the major market indexes, including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite. Micron Technology, Inc. Overview Semiconductors / Technology
------------------------------------------------------------

Micron Technology, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, Malaysia, China, India, and internationally. It operates through the Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU); Core Data Center Business Unit (CDCBU); Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU); and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) segments. The company provides memory products, including dynamic random access memory components and modules, CXL-based memory, LPDDR components and modules, graphics memory, high-bandwidth memory, and data center memory products; multichip packages (MCP) comprising embedded multimedia cards-based, universal flash storage-based, and NAND-based MCPs; and technology leadership products that include 1y DRAM and G9 NAND technologies. It also offers storage products, such as data center solid state drive (SSD), client SSD storage, and auto and industrial SSD storage; managed NAND; NAND flash; NOR flash; and memory cards. In addition, the company provides design tools, including FBGA and part decoder; DRAM power calculators; NAND power calculators; simulation models; chipset compatibility guides; serial presence-detection tools; cross-reference tools; UFSparm; SSD firmware; software and drivers; storage executive software; and obsolete part catalogs. It markets its semiconductor memory and storage products under the Micron and Crucial brands. The company serves the data center, PC, graphics, networking, automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded markets, as well as for smartphone and other mobile-device markets. It sells its products through its direct sales force, independent sales representatives, distributors, and retailers; web-based customer direct sales channel; and channel and distribution partners. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

**Micron Technology (MU): Memory Is the New Gold**
--------------------------------------------------

There’s a quiet revolution happening inside our machines, and it starts with memory. Micron Technology [$MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/) is right at the heart of it.

For decades, the company has been known for making the memory chips that keep our devices running. But now, as artificial intelligence redefines computing, memory has become the new bottleneck… and the new gold.

Micron’s story is one of persistence. Founded in Boise, Idaho, back in 1978, it weathered the brutal ups and downs of the semiconductor cycle for years.

Memory used to be a feast-or-famine business. Prices would spike, then crash.

But that old pattern is fading. AI data centers, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, and next-gen smartphones all demand more memory and faster storage - and once that demand ramps, it rarely turns off.

The company’s results tell the story. Sales are up nearly 49% year-over-year to $37.3 billion and have grown more than 20% over the past three years.

Earnings have exploded: up almost tenfold in just a year. Micron’s profit margin has climbed to 40%.

Those aren’t just cyclical numbers; they’re structural. Cash flow is solid at $1.7 billion, and the balance sheet looks healthy with a debt-to-equity ratio under 30%.

At around 12 times forward earnings, the stock remains one of the cheaper plays in the semiconductor space, despite a market cap of more than $220 billion.

Institutions clearly see the opportunity.

Big institutional investors have taken notice too. Look at the recent flood of inflows into the stock as seen as green bars on this MoneyFlows chart:

Micron has shown up on the MoneyFlows Outlier 20 report 21 times since 2014, a clear sign of steady accumulation. This year, it has appeared 4 times since July:

Big Money is betting that memory will be the lifeblood of AI infrastructure - and Micron has the scale, the technology, and the timing to deliver.

Micron’s MAP Score of 84.5 puts it firmly in buy-zone territory, balancing strong fundamentals with equally strong technicals.

The stock’s strength this year isn’t just a trade; it reflects a shift in how investors view the entire memory industry. Once cyclical, now critical.

**Rating: Long.** Micron is an outlier transforming from a commodity memory maker into a cornerstone of the AI economy.

# Stock Market News: S&P 500 gains, Apple lays off and Crypto miners lead

Here is your daily stock market wrap.

By[Aparajita Chatterjee](https://www.thestreet.com/author/aparajita-chatterjee)

Stocks Writer, The Street

Reviewed by [Dana Sullivan Kilroy](https://www.thestreet.com/author/dana-sullivan-kilroy)

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

## Key Points

* S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose sharply, led by tech and AI-related stocks.
* US-China talks, improved peace prospects, and Trump-Xi meetings boosted investor confidence.
* Bitcoin miners turned AI stocks surged after JPMorgan upgrades.

Good news for investors everywhere, as the week began with significant gains for the [S&P 500](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/s/s-p-500) and the Nasdaq.

* **The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, driven by bullish movements in Broadcom, Robinhood, and Micron.**
* **The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced significant gains from the much-needed [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) push and closed nearly 600 points, or 2.7%, higher.**
* **The Dow Jones Industrial Average was also positive, up 0.4% at the close, and the Russell 2000 closed 1.9% higher.**

After weeks of trepidation surrounding AI and tech stocks, which had mostly fallen, the market opened on a bullish note on Monday, November 24.

The [CBOE](https://www.thestreet.com/quote/CBOE) Volatility Index VIX came at 20, declining nearly 12%, reaffirming investor faith.

In commodities, precious metals Gold and Silver continue to play hide and seek, up 1.4% and 2.6% today, respectively.

Oil regained some of its losses from the past week, up 1.5% but remains under the $60 per barrel mark, as talks of Russia-Ukraine peace deal make progress.

“Is it really possible that big progress is being made in Peace Talks between Russia and Ukraine??? Don’t believe it until you see it, but something good just may be happening,” President Donald Trump posted on his [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/115604227117479754) on Monday.

## US-China talks boost investor confidence

On Monday, President Trump posted that he “had a very good telephone call with President Xi, of China.”

The optimism surrounding the call, which included discussions on fentanyl, soybeans, and the situation in Ukraine and Russia, extended into the market as it reacted positively to the amicability between the two countries.

It was also revealed that Chinese leader Xi has invited President Trump to Beijing, China, in April, which Trump accepted, while President Xi will also visit the US later in 2026.

The talks follow President Trump and Xi’s meeting in October during the [APEC](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/weekly-market-wrap-first-solar-amazon-lead-starbucks-slips) Summit in South Korea, which resulted in a decrease in tariffs, a delay in export controls on rare earths, and a promise to continue buying soybeans from US farmers.

## Crypto miners turn AI Infrastructure plays, see stock rally

Cipher Mining and Iren, two Bitcoin miners turned AI computing power providers, saw a stock surge on Monday with an upgrade from analyst JP Morgan.

**More AI Stocks:**

* [**Is Nvidia’s AI boom already priced in? Oppenheimer doesn’t think so**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/is-nvidias-ai-boom-already-priced-in-oppenheimer-doesnt-think-so)
* [**Windows president told ‘Stop this nonsense. No one wants this’**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/windows-president-told-stop-this-nonsense-no-one-wants-this)
* [**Michael Burry turns up heat on anti-AI bet**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/fund-manager-michael-burry-turns-up-heat-on-anti-ai-bet)
* [**AI plays expanding role in predicting natural disasters**](https://www.thestreet.com/technology/ai-plays-expanding-role-in-predicting-natural-disasters)
* [**Morgan Stanley revamps Nvidia’s price target ahead of big Q3**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/morgan-stanley-revamps-nvidias-price-target-ahead-of-big-q3)
* [**Cathie Wood buys $16.2 million of sinking AI stock**](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/cathie-wood-buys-16-2-million-of-sinking-ai-stock)

Cipher Mining, one of the top S&P 500 performers today, jumped 18%, extending a 260% year-to-date gain buoyed by an upgrade from JPMorgan.

JPMorgan upgraded the stock to Overweight with a price target of $18, up from $12, citing attractive entry levels and the company’s improving position to sign new HPC (high performance compute) deals across approved sites, as reported by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244800).

This upgrade follows Cipher Mining’s announcement on November 20 that it has priced $333 million in additional 7.125% senior secured notes due 2030 through its subsidiary, Cipher Compute LLC, expanding its existing bond program.

The transaction became official today, November 24, 2025, meaning that funds have been transferred to Cipher and new notes delivered to investors.

Latest Business & Market News

## [Apple News loses a longstanding media partner](https://www.thestreet.com/latest-news/apple-news-loses-a-longstanding-media-partner)

Apple News is renegotiating deals and expanding partnerships with news providers.

Aparajita Chatterjee

* [AAPL](/quote/AAPL)

The deal was sold privately to institutional buyers and expands the company’s existing bond program to $1.733 billion.

Cipher [intends](https://investors.ciphermining.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cipher-mining-inc-announces-pricing-333-million-additional) “to use the net proceeds from the offering to finance a portion of the construction costs associated with additional facilities within the Barber Lake Facility, a high-performance computing data center near Colorado City, Texas.”

**Iren,** another bitcoin miner turned [AI contender](https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/irens-ai-ambitions-surge-in-q1-earnings), saw a stock gain of 14.7% on Monday, as a ripple effect of the renewed interest in AI stocks. Additionally, JPMorgan increased its price target to $39 from $28, citing a “flurry of deal activity” and strengthening its integrated cloud valuation assumptions for the target boost, as noted by [TheFly](https://thefly.com/n.php?id=4244812).

## Big tech and energy stock news

Apple’s stock increased 1.6% on Monday, unaffected by the news that it would lose the rights to share CNN stories on its Apple News, as the two media giants renegotiate the terms of their existing deal.

However, later in the day, news came out that Apple had laid off dozens of employees in an attempt to restructure its sales roles, [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-24/apple-aapl-cuts-jobs-across-its-sales-organization-in-rare-layoff). A rarity for the tech giant, the people affected by the job include account managers serving major businesses and people operating Apple’s briefing centers.

In an official statement, Apple noted that it continues to hire for new roles, and those affected can still apply. The company’s stock was declining after hours.

Separately, in a government-led push into private energy markets, the **US plans to buy and own up to 10 new large nuclear reactors**, funded through Japan’s $550 billion commitment announced in October, according to [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-19/us-to-own-reactors-stemming-from-japan-s-550-billion-pledge).

Carl Coe, the Department of Energy chief of staff, said that as much as $80 billion could be used to construct new reactors built by Westinghouse Electric. Coe was quoted during an energy conference hosted by the Tennessee Advanced Energy Business Council on November 20.

The increase in nuclear reactors serving as energy providers is linked to the rise of data centers and their associated, increasingly growing power demands for AI computing.

The stock of companies in the nuclear energy space, such as Oklo, NuScale Power, Constellation Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all saw an uptick in trading on Monday.

attributes.gen_ai.prompt.0.content:
You are a strict financial data quality evaluator for Micron research.
            Hold the research to the full EXCELLENT standard.
            
            **EVALUATION CRITERIA:**
            
            1. **COMPLETENESS CHECK** (Must have ALL of these):
               ✓ Current stock price with exact dollar amount and percentage change
               ✓ Latest quarterly EPS with actual vs estimate comparison
               ✓ Latest quarterly revenue with actual vs estimate comparison  
               ✓ At least 3 recent financial news items with dates and sources
               ✓ Key financial metrics (P/E ratio, market cap)
               ✓ All data has proper source citations with URLs
            
            2. **ACCURACY CHECK**:
               ✓ Numbers are specific (not "around" or "approximately")
               ✓ Dates are recent and clearly stated
               ✓ Sources are credible financial websites
               ✓ No conflicting information without explanation
            
            3. **CURRENCY CHECK**:
               ✓ Stock price data is from today or latest trading day
               ✓ Earnings data is from most recent quarter
               ✓ News items are from last 7 days (or most recent available)
            
            **RATING GUIDELINES:**
            
            - **EXCELLENT**: All criteria met perfectly, comprehensive data, multiple source verification
            - **GOOD**: All required data present, good quality sources, minor gaps acceptable
            - **FAIR**: Most required data present but missing some elements or has quality issues
            - **POOR**: Missing critical data (stock price, earnings, or major sources), unreliable sources
            
            **EVALUATION OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            
            COMPLETENESS: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            - Stock price data: [Present/Missing] - [Details]
            - Earnings data: [Present/Missing] - [Details]  
            - News coverage: [Present/Missing] - [Details]
            - Financial metrics: [Present/Missing] - [Details]
            - Source quality: [Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor] - [Details]
            
            ACCURACY: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            - Data specificity: [Comments]
            - Source credibility: [Comments]
            - Data consistency: [Comments]
            
            CURRENCY: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            - Stock data recency: [Comments]
            - Earnings recency: [Comments]
            - News recency: [Comments]
            
            OVERALL RATING: [EXCELLENT/GOOD/FAIR/POOR]
            
            **IMPROVEMENT FEEDBACK:**
            [Specific instructions for what needs to be improved, added, or fixed]
            [If rating is below GOOD, provide exact search queries needed]
            [List any missing data points that must be found]
            
            **CRITICAL RULE**: If ANY of these are missing, overall rating cannot exceed FAIR:
            - Exact current stock price with change
            - Latest quarterly EPS actual vs estimate  
            - Latest quarterly revenue actual vs estimate
            - At least 2 credible news sources from recent period

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

![Terry Lane]()
![Terry Lane](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/ndol2zcoNBDh-qImvkfrfdtkIAI=/200x200/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/TerryHeadshotcrop-2e42cd194b404f6da48715967dd2c5de.jpg)

Terry Lane is a writer for Investopedia with 25 years of experience in journalism and communications. He covers personal finance, Congress, government regulations, and economics.

![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)
![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)

David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

### TipRanks Black Friday Sale

* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.
* [Subscribe to TipRanks' Smart Investor Picks](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-smartinvestor/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  and see our data in action through our high-performing model portfolio -  now also 60% off

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

# What to Expect in Markets This Week: Retail Sales; Earnings From Deere, Dell and Alibaba; and Thanksgiving

![Terry Lane]()
![Terry Lane](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/ndol2zcoNBDh-qImvkfrfdtkIAI=/200x200/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/TerryHeadshotcrop-2e42cd194b404f6da48715967dd2c5de.jpg)

Terry Lane is a writer for Investopedia with 25 years of experience in journalism and communications. He covers personal finance, Congress, government regulations, and economics.

![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)

David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.
