# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

### TipRanks Black Friday Sale

* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.
* [Subscribe to TipRanks' Smart Investor Picks](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-smartinvestor/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  and see our data in action through our high-performing model portfolio -  now also 60% off

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

![Shoppers carry Macy's and Nordstrom bags at Broadway Plaza in Walnut Creek, California, US, on Monday, Dec. 16, 2024. ](https://www.investopedia.com/thmb/X7cBgb3UXBXjZxXYJeArrBuZ0GU=/1500x0/filters:no_upscale():max_bytes(150000):strip_icc()/GettyImages-2189857282-0858fde2ba3a48c09eb1b9953d94560d.jpg)

David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

### TipRanks Black Friday Sale

* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

# The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro & Markets, November 23, 2025

[Ran Melamed](/news/author/ran-melamedtipranks-com)

## **Everything to Know about Macro and Markets**

U.S. stocks ended the week mixed as investors balanced strong corporate earnings with renewed volatility in tech and crypto. The S&P 500 **[(SPX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/spx)** gained 0.98%, the [Nasdaq 100](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100) **[(NDX)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/nasdaq-100)** added 0.77%, and the [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones) **[(DJIA)](https://www.tipranks.com/index/dow-jones)** advanced 1.08%. [Bitcoin](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd) **[(BTC-USD)](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency/btc-usd)** climbed 1.43% to $85,892 after a turbulent few days.

* [Claim 60% off TipRanks Premium](https://lp.tipranks.com/blackfriday-2025-b-premium/?coupon=BKFRCYMN2025P60&llf=rss&timer=on)  for the data-backed insights and research tools you need to invest with confidence.

Energy shares lagged as oil prices **[(CL)](https://www.tipranks.com/commodities/cm:cl)** fell more than 2% on news that the U.S. is pushing a peace proposal between Russia and Ukraine. Airlines gained from lower fuel costs. Southwest Airlines [(LUV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv) [rose 5.26%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/luv), while Delta Air Lines [(DAL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal) [increased 4.65%](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dal).

The latest U.S. jobs report showed stronger-than-expected growth. The [economy added 119,000 jobs in September](https://www.tipranks.com/economic-indicators), while unemployment edged up to 4.4%. Following the data, traders saw only a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate cut in December, down from 90% one month ago. Treasury yields held near 4.15%, and the U.S. Dollar Index stayed steady.

## **Nvidia’s Strong Results Couldn’t Stop the Slide**

The main story last week surrounded **Nvidia’s** [(NVDA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda) [third-quarter earnings report](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nvda/forecast), as the market was in desperate need of strong results. Nvidia indeed rose to the occasion, providing some relief to investors. Nvidia posted an impressive quarter, reporting revenue of $57 billion, up 62% year over year. The company’s data center sales reached $51 billion, driven by rising demand for its new Blackwell processors, while Chief Executive Jensen Huang stated demand remains “off the charts.”

Despite the strong results, Nvidia’s shares fell 3.1% as investors rotated away from large-cap tech stocks. The decline came after an early 5% surge in morning trading. Other chipmakers also lost ground, including **Micron Technology** [(MU)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mu), **Lam Research** [(LRCX)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lrcx), and data analytics company **Palantir** [(PLTR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/pltr).

The reversal followed the jobs report, which dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts. Analysts said the pullback shows investors are becoming cautious about the pace and cost of the [AI](https://www.tipranks.com/compare-stocks/artificial-intelligence) buildout, even as major tech firms continue to invest heavily.

## **Stocks That Made the Week**

While Nvidia’s strong earnings sparked optimism about AI’s long-term prospects, smaller AI-related stocks had a tougher week. **CoreWeave** [(CRWV)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/crwv) fell 7.6%, **Nebius** [(NBIS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nbis) dropped almost 11%, and **IREN** [(IREN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/iren) declined 5%. These GPU-focused data center firms rely on Nvidia’s hardware and have faced mounting pressure since mid-November.

Bitcoin miners turned AI players, such as **Cipher Mining** [(CIFR)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cifr) and IREN, also slid as investors grew wary of speculative names. **Bloom Energy** [(BE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/be) and **Oklo** [(OKLO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/oklo) both moved lower, reflecting shrinking risk appetite across the AI sector.

In contrast, **Eli Lilly** [(LLY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/lly) reached a market value of $1 trillion, joining **Apple** [(AAPL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/aapl), Nvidia, and **Berkshire Hathaway** **[(BRK.A)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.a)** **[(BRK.B)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/brk.b)** in the exclusive group. The pharmaceutical company’s success was driven by its weight-loss drugs, Mounjaro and Zepbound, which continue to see high demand. Lilly is now the only non-technology company, bar Berkshire, with a valuation above $1 trillion.

In other news, **Opendoor Technologies** [(OPEN)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) [jumped 9.58% to $6.75](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/open) after DE Shaw disclosed a 6.4% stake in the online real estate firm. The move echoed a similar rally earlier this year after Jane Street revealed its own position. However, analysts noted that DE Shaw’s stake likely came through a statistical arbitrage fund rather than a long-term investment strategy. Still, the news boosted sentiment in the housing tech space, especially after New York Fed President John Williams hinted at a December rate cut.

Also in the spotlight, **AST SpaceMobile** [(ASTS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) [rose 1.32% to $52.09](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/asts) after announcing plans to launch its next-generation satellite, Bluebird 6, next month. The larger satellite is designed to improve data transmission in support of the company’s goal of providing broadband access directly to smartphones from space. The announcement lifted peers such as **EchoStar** [(SATS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/sats) and **Rocket Lab** [(RKLB)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/rklb), as investor interest in “services from space” companies remained high despite their ongoing losses.

## **Crypto’s Rough Week**

**Bitcoin** fell below $81,000 midweek, hitting its lowest level since April before rebounding. The drop triggered more than $2 billion in [crypto](https://www.tipranks.com/cryptocurrency) liquidations, mostly from long positions. Bitcoin ETFs saw $903 million in outflows on Thursday alone, one of the largest since their debut.

The total crypto market value declined to $2.85 trillion from $4.3 trillion in early October. Analysts said support remains near $75,000, but sentiment has weakened. Citi analysts described the downturn as “a bit of a meltdown,” adding that investor flows are unlikely to recover quickly.

## **Upcoming Earnings and Dividend Announcements**

The earnings calendar remains full this week, with major names from technology, retail, and industrials set to report.

On Monday, **Li Auto** [(LI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/li) will open the week with results, offering insight into electric vehicle demand in China following recent price competition. **Deere** [(DE)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/de) will also report, with investors watching for updates on global equipment demand and agricultural exports.

On Tuesday, **Alibaba** [(BABA)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/baba) will headline, with Wall Street focused on trends in e-commerce and cloud revenue. **Dell Technologies** [(DELL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/dell) and **Zscaler** [(ZS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/zs) will also release results, which should provide a closer look at enterprise spending and cybersecurity budgets heading into year-end.

Wednesday will bring reports from **Autodesk** [(ADSK)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adsk) and **Workday** [(WDAY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/wday), both key indicators of software demand among large companies. Meanwhile, **Best Buy** [(BBY)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bby) and **Analog Devices** [(ADI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/adi) will give updates on consumer electronics and chip inventories, helping gauge holiday retail momentum.

Later in the week, **HP** [(HPQ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/hpq), **Nio** [(NIO)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nio), and **Semtech** [(SMTC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/smtc) will round out the lineup. Together, these reports will cover sectors ranging from PCs to electric vehicles to semiconductors, providing a broad snapshot of market and business sentiment ahead of December.

### **Ex-Dividend Dates This Week**

Several notable companies will trade ex-dividend in the coming days, offering opportunities for income-focused investors.

On Monday, **Johnson & Johnson** [(JNJ)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jnj) and **Vertiv Holdings** [(VRT)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/vrt) will go ex-dividend. Johnson & Johnson’s $1.30 payout represents a 2.49% yield, while Vertiv will pay $0.06 per share.

Tuesday brings **S&P Global** [(SPGI)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/spgi) with a $0.96 dividend and a strong buy rating, and **CDW** [(CDW)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/cdw) with a $0.63 payout. **Xylem** [(XYL)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/xyl) will also trade ex-dividend, with a 1.11% yield.

On Wednesday, **T-Mobile US** [(TMUS)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/tmus) will lead with a $1.02 dividend, joined by **Newmont Mining** [(NEM)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/nem) and **Manulife Financial** [(MFC)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/mfc). Later in the week, **Realty Income** [(O)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/o) and **Brookfield Renewable Partners** [(BEP)](https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/bep) will close out the list with yields above 5%, continuing their steady monthly distributions.

These payouts span industries from telecom to financials to renewable energy, showing continued consistency in shareholder returns through the final quarter of 2025.

This trading week is—Thankfully—shorter than usual. But there's still work to do.

Stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday. But the week will still bring several economic releases, along with earnings reports from companies including John Deere, Alibaba, Applied Digital and Dell Technologies.

The September report on U.S. retail sales, delayed by the government shutdown, will be released just ahead of [Black Friday](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/b/blackfriday.asp), one of the busiest shopping days of the year. Weekly jobless claims, pending home sales, durable-goods orders and the latest consumer confidence survey are also on time. Some data originally scheduled for this week will be delayed as government statistical agencies update their timetables to catch up on [reports that were delayed](https://www.investopedia.com/government-shutdown-ties-longest-in-u-s-history-11843303) during government shutdown.

In addition to the day off Thursday, stock markets will close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. ET.

Read to the bottom for our calendar of key events—and one more thing.

## John Deere, Dell, Alibaba Highlight Shortened Earnings Week

Investors on Monday will get an update from laboratory equipment maker Agilent, video call firm Zoom, and Symbotic, a [partner of Walmart](https://www.investopedia.com/symbotic-walmart-announce-deals-to-extend-robotics-automation-partnership-8775532) that makes AI-powered warehouse automation products.

Tuesday is also busy: [Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba](https://www.investopedia.com/alibaba-shares-jump-on-plan-to-boost-ai-spending-beyond-53b-11816017), chipmaker Applied Digital, [design software maker Autodesk](https://www.investopedia.com/autodesk-REDACTED), data storage provider NetApp, and [cybersecurity firm Zscaler](https://www.investopedia.com/zscaler-stock-leads-nasdaq-gainers-thursday-11692331) are scheduled to report earnings. Workday is expected to report quarterly earnings for the first time since activist investment group Elliott Investment Management reported [taking a stake in the company](https://www.investopedia.com/workday-stock-jumps-as-activist-investor-elliott-takes-usd2-billion-stake-praises-management-plan-11811691).

Dell Technologies and HP are slated to report on Tuesday after the computer and equipment makers were [downgraded by analysts](https://www.investopedia.com/why-dell-technologies-stock-is-plunging-to-lead-s-and-p-500-decliners-monday-dell-hpe-hpq-11850671) who see the companies struggling with higher costs for components. John Deere’s report on Wednesday is likely to provide some insight into the overall health of the [construction and agriculture industries](https://www.investopedia.com/deere-lowers-profit-outlook-in-challenging-economic-environment-11790751).

## Retail Sales to Roll In Ahead of Black Friday

[Delayed retail-sales results](https://www.investopedia.com/with-shutdown-over-when-will-key-economic-data-come-out-11848852) for September, due Tuesday, will show whether shoppers kept up their momentum going into the shutdown as consumers focus their attention on Black Friday and the holiday season. Market watchers will also get a look at inflation with the release of the wholesale-focused Producer Price Index for September.

Reports from private-sector groups will provide updates on pending home sales and consumer confidence in November. Weekly jobless claims are also expected to be issued Wednesday and are likely of interest after last week’s [employment report showed hiring surged](https://www.investopedia.com/job-creation-accelerated-back-in-september-but-so-did-unemployment-11853461).

Several reports on the calendar this week will be rescheduled, including the first reading of third-quarter [gross domestic product](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/what-is-gdp-why-its-important-to-economists-investors/), the October [PCE Price Index](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/pce.asp), and the advanced reports on October trade balance, retail inventories, and wholesale inventories. The delayed data could make matters more difficult for Federal Reserve officials, who are scheduled to issue their [next interest rate decision](https://www.investopedia.com/why-the-fed-s-next-interest-rate-move-is-becoming-so-hard-to-predict-11851839) on Dec. 10.

               Search: "Micron latest quarterly earnings results"
               Search: "Micron earnings vs estimates beat miss"
               Extract: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, beat/miss percentages
            
            3. **Recent Financial News**:
               Search: "Micron financial news latest week"
               Search: "Micron analyst ratings upgrade downgrade"
               Extract: Provide 5 recent, well-sourced headlines.
            
            4. **Financial Metrics**:
               Search: "Micron PE ratio market cap financial metrics"
               Extract: P/E ratio, market cap, key financial ratios
            
            **OUTPUT FORMAT:**
            Organize your findings in these exact sections:
            
            ## CURRENT MARKET DATA
            - Stock Price: $XXX.XX (±X.XX, ±X.X%)
            - Trading Volume: X.X million (vs avg X.X million)
            - 52-Week Range: $XXX.XX - $XXX.XX
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## LATEST EARNINGS
            - EPS: $X.XX actual vs $X.XX estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Revenue: $XXX billion actual vs $XXX billion estimate (beat/miss by X%)
            - Year-over-Year Growth: X%
            - Quarter: QX YYYY
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            ## RECENT NEWS (Last 7 Days)
            1. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            2. [Headline] - [Date] - [Source] - [Impact: Positive/Negative/Neutral]
            3. [Continue until you reach the required number of items]
            
            ## KEY FINANCIAL METRICS
            - P/E Ratio: XX.X
            - Market Cap: $XXX billion
            - [Other available metrics]
            - Source: [URL and date]
            
            **CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:**
            - Use EXACT figures, not approximations
            - Include source URLs for verification
            - Note data timestamps/dates
            - If any section is missing data, explicitly state what couldn't be found

               ✓ Current stock price with exact dollar amount and percentage change
